subject: Follow-up: prompt data landing, visibility & retention — next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@clarityhealth.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: prompt data landing, visibility & retention — next steps

Hi Samira — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and 3 follow-ups we promised: 

Recap (1 line): you want an LLM-assisted triage layer that will receive clinician-entered text (freeform visit notes + structured fields) and return suggested routing and short summaries, with strict limits on any stored patient-identifiable content.

Items I/O:
- Can you confirm the exact fields you consider PII/PHI versus non-sensitive (example: patient name, MRN, DOB, direct identifiers = PII; symptom text anonymized = non-PII unless name present).
- Residency requirement: you mentioned EU residency for analytics and audit logs; is that requirement for all persisted logs or only for backups/audit exports?
- Retention policy ask: you mentioned two buckets — (A) operational troubleshooting logs (short window) and (B) audit/history (multi-year). Please confirm the retention windows we should design for each.

What I can share now (summary): 
- Hosted API: prompts/outputs are not retained for product improvement by default unless a customer opts into sharing; operational traces (request metadata for billing/health) are retained short-term for troubleshooting.
- Dedicated / Private deploys: we can run with prompt/output no-store by default; retention policies are configurable and can be enforced by your infra/KMS.
- We support a per-route flag (no_store) and a request-level header to opt-out of prompt/output persistence; we can also enable automatic redaction of fields using a customer-provided PII schema.

Attachments: sending a short retention overview + draft DPA + SOC2 summary for your security team.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Quick security sync with Naomi from our compliance team (30 min) — are you available tomorrow or Wednesday?
2) You send the list of fields you classify as PII/PHI and the two target retention windows (troubleshooting / audit).
3) We’ll return a proposed config (per-route no_store + EU-residency routing + audit export plan) and a redlined DPA for review.

Thanks — Karthik

--

From: Samira Khan <samira@clarityhealth.ai>

Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 14:37:12 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt data landing, visibility & retention — next steps

Thanks Karthik — quick answers below to unblock the config work.

PII/PHI classification (high level):
- Always PII/PHI: patient full name, MRN, national ID, SSN, email, phone, exact DOB.
- Conditional PII: clinician notes that contain identifiers (e.g., “Mr. Smith with MRN 12345”); freeform symptoms text is OK to process if identifiers are redacted.

Residency: EU residency requirement applies to any persisted prompt/output or transaction logs that could be reconstructed into patient-level events. Billing records that only contain line-item metering without identifiers can remain in US.

Retention windows:
- Operational troubleshooting logs: max 14 days. Must be deletable on demand.
- Audit/history exports: must be exportable and storable for 7 years by our auditors (we do not require you to store 7 years, we need a mechanism to export sanitized audit records regularly to our EU S3).

Questions / constraints for Redwood:
1) Can you provide a configuration where hosted calls with our public API token never persist prompt or generated output at rest in Redwood systems?
2) Is there an automated redaction/preprocessing hook that we can run client-side or at the edge before the request reaches the model?
3) For Dedicated/Private: confirm there is no product feature that sends telemetry off-cluster (we require no exfil for private installs).

We’re available for a security call tomorrow at 15:00 PT if that works — Samira + one of our compliance engineers will join.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Product, ClarityHealth AI
samira@clarityhealth.ai
+44 20 7946 0871

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@clarityhealth.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: prompt data landing, visibility & retention — next steps

Samira — great detail, thanks. Short answers and proposed constraints below. I’m copying Naomi to pick up the security call and the DPA redline.

Answers / proposed configuration:
- Hosted API: by default we do not persist prompt/outputs for product improvement unless explicitly enabled by customers. For your use case we can enable a token-level policy "no_store=true" which will prevent any prompt/output payloads from being written to persistent storage in our hosted environment; operational traces (headers, timestamps, model id, response latency) are retained for 14 days for billing and incident triage and can be configured to be routed to an EU bucket when requested.
- Edge/client-side redaction: we offer a lightweight SDK preprocessor (JS/Python) that runs an allowlist/redaction step before transmission, plus model-side dynamic redaction rules that can be applied via a per-route PII schema. We’ll include the SDK snippet in the security brief.
- Dedicated / Private: no telemetry leaves the customer cluster by default — any optional telemetry export to Redwood-managed services is opt-in and documented in the installation guide. For on-prem, we can ship the service with telemetry disabled and provide admin-facing toggles.
- Export for audits: we can provide an export hook to push sanitized audit artifacts to your EU S3 on a scheduled basis (you control the sanitization rules). That satisfies the 7-year audit retention because the artifacts are under your control.

Attachments included in this thread: redwood-data-retention-overview.pdf (high-level), DPA-DRAFT-ClarityHealth.docx (initial redline), SOC2-Type2-summary.pdf (summary evidence).

Proposed next steps (short timeline):
- Naomi to run a 30-min security call today at 15:00 PT (she’s copied) — confirm.
- You share the minimal PII field list (you already gave a good start) and we’ll propose a per-route config with examples (no_store + EU-routing + preprocessor).
- We’ll return a redlined DPA within 3 business days and a config snippet you can test in a staging token.

Naomi — can you pick this up with Samira? I can join if helpful.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
